clue.text: Pass by failing to fail

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lapse is a failing or slip

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes through an exam merely by not managing to fail it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' and 'fail' look like exam opposites; 'Pass' is a mountain col and 'fail' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to break down or give way, a synonym of failing.

clue.text: Bit of bacon some won't eat — rejected if not Danish, primarily

definitions.text: Bit of bacon some won't eat

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Bacon rind gets left on the plate, unless the bacon happens to be Danish.
explanation.walkthrough: Danish bacon is a familiar British supermarket brand, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin of a bacon rasher, often cut off and left uneaten.

clue.text: Transported coal in another fuel container

indicators.note: transported, as in carried away or moved about, says the letters of coal in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coal is carried about in a container meant for some other fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Coal is one fuel, so 'another fuel' is oil: the container is for oil rather than coal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilcan holds oil, a fuel other than the coal named in the surface.

clue.text: Rock night broadcast, with Yes playing first

indicators.note: first puts the jumbled Yes ahead of the other piece
playing suggests the letters of Yes are performing in a new arrangement
broadcast means the word is spoken on air, so its sound is wanted

parts.note: night sounds like nite

explanation.surface: A radio station plays rock at night, with the band Yes on first.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes is a British prog-rock band, so 'Rock' and 'playing' both fit the music picture. 'broadcast' gives NITE, a sound-alike of night; 'playing' shuffles YES to SYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Syenite is a coarse-grained igneous rock similar to granite.

clue.text: 'Small beer' — second fellow's description of Miller's Willy

parts.note: ale is a beer
a fellow is a man; the 's joins the piece to what follows

explanation.surface: A man describes Miller's Willy dismissively as small beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy is Willy Loman, hero of Arthur Miller's play Death of a Salesman; 'Small beer' (something trivial) is the misleading phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Loman is the travelling salesman of Arthur Miller's tragedy, so that is how he is described.

clue.text: Behind short film supporting revised rate for hearing aid

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it
revised says the letters of rate are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a rump is a behind, the backside
ET is short for the film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A cinema advertising a short film boosts a revised entry price for its hearing-aid users.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns RATE into EART; 'supporting' puts ET under RUMP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is the old horn-shaped device held to the ear to help the hard of hearing.

clue.text: Lines up outside No 10 — speech just beginning

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole build is read bottom to top
outside means these pieces wrap around the abbreviation for number

parts.note: ten is the number 10

indicators.note: just beginning asks for only the opening letter of speech

parts.note: No is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Journalists line up outside No 10 Downing Street as a prime-ministerial speech begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps TEN plus S around NO, making TENNOS, and 'up' turns it over. No 10 Downing Street is the British prime minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, so lines of verse stand for it.

clue.text: Lack of talent not a feature of Lord's

indicators.note: not before a says that letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: lack of talent is no ability

explanation.surface: Talent is lacking at Lord's, the cricket ground, perhaps a dig at a poor team.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground; here it means belonging to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble rank is a defining quality of a peer, so it is what a lord possesses.

clue.text: Flower shop online here?

definitions.meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: A florist asks whether the flower can be bought online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river: something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is a South American river and also the name of the online retail giant.

clue.text: Foul-smelling old hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: An old hat has gone smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare literary word meaning rank or stinking.

clue.text: Short piece needing correction, with name for one composer finally changed

indicators.note: changed says the resulting letters are rearranged
for one means a single letter is swapped for the new one
finally asks for the last letter of composer

explanation.surface: A composer's short piece needs correcting, with the name altered at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks R, the last of composer; 'for one' swaps one R of CORRECTION for N, and 'changed' shuffles the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertino is a short or small-scale concerto, a brief musical work.

clue.text: Part of Manhattan, as far as two quarters will get you

parts.note: as far as means up to
W and N are two compass quarters, west and north

explanation.surface: Fifty cents buys you a ride to some part of Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter is also a US 25-cent coin, which gives the surface its fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptown is the northern, residential district of Manhattan in New York.

clue.text: No longer called brother that's not working

definitions.meaning: a monk who has left his religious order is out of it, and no longer addressed as Brother

explanation.surface: A monk who has left the monastery is no longer called brother, and something has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of order means broken down, and also literally outside a monastic order.

clue.text: Name given to male deer, say? Originally, the ungulates in some faraway place

parts.note: Tim is a given name

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, which sounds like buk

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone names a stag, then wonders about the deer in some remote land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives BUK, a sound-alike of buck; 'Originally' takes T and U from 'the ungulates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbuktu, a city in Mali, is proverbial for the remotest place imaginable.

clue.text: Organised whole of largest alto section

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a larger thing, so the answer is a run inside largest alto

explanation.surface: The biggest part of a choir, the alto section, is well organised.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the gap in 'larGEST ALTo'; alto and section suggest a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A gestalt is a pattern or structure perceived as a unified whole, more than its parts.

clue.text: Attacked an idol with tie clip? That's 13

indicators.note: 13 is out of order, so the letters are put out of their order
to clip is to trim, so tie loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a pop idol with a tie clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's 13' points to the answer at 13, OUT OF ORDER, as the signal to shuffle AN IDOL plus TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid into is an idiom for attacked vigorously, physically or with words.

clue.text: Veiled criticism of bargain gin supply

parts.note: a snip is a bargain

indicators.note: supply read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters of gin bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Cheap gin is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but read it as 'in a supple way' to see that it shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniping is sly, indirect sniping remarks, criticism delivered from cover.

clue.text: Cell deaths topped small number Puck's got cross about

indicators.note: topped means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: one is a small number

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: cross is taken as the word itself
Puck is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Puck is cross about cell deaths caused by some small number.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Puck's' is simply I; 'topped' beheads the small number and 'about' wraps the cross around that I.
explanation.definitionFit: Necrosis is the death of cells or tissue through injury or disease.

clue.text: Fool includes certain guarantees

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A fool's guarantees include some that are certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to promise or guarantee that something is so.

clue.text: Stupid people undone by this flaw?

indicators.note: undone suggests something unravelled, so the letters of this flaw are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some fools are undone by a particular flaw: their stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Halfwits is an insult for foolish or dim people.

clue.text: Gripped by sudden fear, topless opponents in game lacking vital element

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the other piece
topless says the top letter is removed

parts.note: panic is sudden fear
O and X are the opposing players in noughts and crosses

explanation.surface: Players in a game, gripped by panic, find themselves short of something vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' beheads the sudden fear and 'Gripped by' sets the two players inside. Noughts and crosses is the British name for tic-tac-toe, the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoxic means lacking oxygen, the element vital for life.

clue.text: White chairs partially with designs using steel, glass and plastic, say

definitions.text: designs using steel, glass and plastic, say

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words white chairs is used

explanation.surface: White chairs feature in modern designs made of steel, glass and plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles 'wHITE CHairs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech is a style of architecture and interior design that uses industrial materials such as steel and glass.

clue.text: Where kippers can be found on vacation in Harwich

parts.note: emptying Harwich of its inner letters leaves just its two outer letters, each named by the same NATO radio-alphabet code word

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in Harwich find smoked fish on the breakfast menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Harwich is an Essex port. Vacated, it leaves HH, and H is Hotel in the radio alphabet. A kipper is a smoked herring, but here it is someone having a kip, a sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels are where sleepers, people having a kip, spend the night.

clue.text: Device that prevents pouring out of claret

definitions.text: Device that prevents pouring out of claret

parts.words: Device that prevents pouring out of claret
parts.note: claret is slang for blood, so this is a device that stops bleeding rather than a wine stopper

explanation.surface: A gadget that stops red wine being poured.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is old British boxing slang for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourniquet is a band tightened round a limb to stop bleeding from a wound.

clue.text: Nought drunk by small child? Just a little Coke

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed inside the other piece

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nought is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A toddler drinks nothing but a little cola.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke here is cocaine, not the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is slang for a single snort of cocaine, a small amount.

clue.text: One form of pasta if potato, say, is short

indicators.note: is short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a potato is an example of a tuber

explanation.surface: A potato dish might count as pasta if short of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubes are a common pasta shape, as in penne or rigatoni.

clue.text: Mum let sin get out of control

indicators.note: letters that get out of control run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother lets sin run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it means keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum, as in 'keep mum', means saying nothing, quiet.

clue.text: Sadly risible, keeping Times owner's name inscribed in book here

definitions.text: owner's name inscribed in book here

indicators.note: keeping means the shuffled letters hold the other piece inside
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of risible are rearranged

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A laughable item kept by The Times bears its owner's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' shuffles RISIBLE to ELIBRIS; 'keeping' puts X inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris, Latin for 'from the books of', introduces a bookplate naming the owner.
